## Proof

**Answer leak check:** The problem statement contains only the problem setup and the question. No solution, proof sketch, answer value, or formalization notes are present. Proceeding.

**Claim.** Yes, such a constant $M\geq 0$ exists.

**Proof.** Define the map
$$T:\ell_p(A)\to \ell_p(A),\qquad T(f)=\big(\theta_a(f)\big)_{a\in A}.$$
By hypothesis, for every $f\in\ell_p(A)$ we have $\sum_{a\in A}|\theta_a(f)|^p<\infty$, so $T(f)\in\ell_p(A)$; that is, $T$ is well-defined on all of $\ell_p(A)$. It is plainly linear. The desired inequality $\|f\|_\theta\leq M\|f\|$ is exactly the statement that $T$ is a bounded linear operator, since $\|f\|_\theta=\|T(f)\|_{\ell_p}$.

Since $1\leq p<\infty$, the space $\ell_p(A)$ is a Banach space (it is complete, including for infinite $A$). We show $T$ has closed graph; the Closed Graph Theorem then yields boundedness.

**Closed graph.** Suppose $f_n\to f$ in $\ell_p(A)$ and $T(f_n)\to g$ in $\ell_p(A)$. We must show $g=T(f)$, i.e. $g_a=\theta_a(f)$ for every $a\in A$.

Fix $a\in A$. Each $\theta_a$ is a bounded (hence continuous) linear functional on $\ell_p(A)$, so
$$\theta_a(f_n)\to \theta_a(f)\quad\text{as }n\to\infty.$$
On the other hand, $T(f_n)\to g$ in $\ell_p(A)$ implies coordinatewise convergence, so in particular the $a$-th coordinate satisfies
$$(T(f_n))_a=\theta_a(f_n)\to g_a.$$
Uniqueness of limits in $\mathbb{R}$ gives $g_a=\theta_a(f)$ for this $a$. Since $a\in A$ was arbitrary, $g=T(f)$.

Thus the graph of $T$ is closed. By the Closed Graph Theorem, $T$ is bounded: there exists $M\geq 0$ with
$$\|T(f)\|_{\ell_p}\leq M\|f\|_{\ell_p}\quad\text{for all }f\in\ell_p(A),$$
which is precisely $\|f\|_\theta\leq M\|f\|$ for all $f\in\ell_p(A)$. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
